stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

options.text: Use 'ueber' to open the locative relative clause.
Use 'auf' to open the locative relative clause.
Use 'in' to open the locative relative clause.
Use 'fuer' to open the locative relative clause.

questions.explanation: In' is the natural locative preposition here, governing dative for static location. The key is C, "Use 'in' to open the locative relative clause". Option A ("Use 'ueber' to open the locative relative clause") is wrong: chooses topic preposition for place. Option B ("Use 'auf' to open the locative relative clause") is wrong: chooses wrong locative preposition. Option D ("Use 'fuer' to open the locative relative clause") is wrong: chooses purpose preposition for place.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: Word order in a subordinate clause with two verbs
questions.learningObjective: Explain verb order with a modal and infinitive in a subordinate clause

stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

options.text: Move 'muss' to second position after the subject.
Place 'muss' before 'lesen' at the end.
Place both verbs before the subject.
Place 'lesen' before 'muss' at the end.

questions.explanation: In a subordinate clause with a modal, the infinitive precedes the finite modal at the end. The key is D, "Place 'lesen' before 'muss' at the end". Option A ("Move 'muss' to second position after the subject") is wrong: applies main-clause order. Option B ("Place 'muss' before 'lesen' at the end") is wrong: reverses modal and infinitive. Option C ("Place both verbs before the subject") is wrong: breaks subordinate clause order.
questions.hint: Infinitive before modal at the end.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: Konjunktiv I without a distinct form
questions.learningObjective: Recognize identical Konjunktiv I and indicative forms in plural

stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

options.text: It implies Konjunktiv I is always identical in all forms.
options.misconception: selects "It implies Konjunktiv I is always identical in all…" where the rule in the passage requires a different condition

options.text: It implies no distinct Konjunktiv I form exists here.
It implies the sentence must use the imperative.
It implies reported speech is impossible here.

questions.explanation: For this plural form, Konjunktiv I equals the indicative, so no distinct form exists. The key is B, "It implies no distinct Konjunktiv I form exists here". Option A ("It implies Konjunktiv I is always identical in all forms") is wrong: selects "It implies Konjunktiv I is always identical in all…" where the rule in the passage requires a different condition. Option C ("It implies the sentence must use the imperative") is wrong: confuses mood categories. Option D ("It implies reported speech is impossible here") is wrong: overstates the limitation.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: A relative clause with a preposition
questions.learningObjective: Explain preposition placement in a formal relative clause

stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

answer.exemplar: Formal German places the preposition before the relative pronoun to make the governed case immediately visible and keep the clause compact.

questions.explanation: Leading preposition marks the case clearly and is preferred in formal tickets. The key value is Formal German places the preposition before the relative pronoun to make the governed case immediately visible and keep the clause compact..
questions.hint: Lead with the preposition for clarity.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: A relative pronoun in the dative
questions.learningObjective: Choose the dative relative pronoun for a masculine antecedent

stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

options.text: Use 'das' as the masculine dative relative pronoun.
Use 'der' as the masculine dative relative pronoun.
Use 'dem' for the masculine dative relative pronoun.
Use 'denen' as the masculine dative relative pronoun.

questions.explanation: Masculine dative relative pronoun is 'dem. The key is C, "Use 'dem' for the masculine dative relative pronoun". Option A ("Use 'das' as the masculine dative relative pronoun") is wrong: uses nominative/accusative form. Option B ("Use 'der' as the masculine dative relative pronoun") is wrong: uses feminine dative form. Option D ("Use 'denen' as the masculine dative relative pronoun") is wrong: uses plural dative form.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: A demonstrative pronoun in a subordinate clause
questions.learningObjective: Use a demonstrative pronoun in a subordinate clause correctly

stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

options.text: Use 'welcher' as a relative pronoun for the bug.
Use 'jener' to point to the named bug.
options.misconception: uses distant demonstrative for near reference

options.text: Use 'er' as a simple pronoun for the bug.
Use 'dieser' to point to the named bug.

questions.explanation: Dieser' clearly points to the specific item just mentioned. The key is D, "Use 'dieser' to point to the named bug". Option A ("Use 'welcher' as a relative pronoun for the bug") is wrong: confuses relative with demonstrative. Option B ("Use 'jener' to point to the named bug") is wrong: uses distant demonstrative for near reference. Option C ("Use 'er' as a simple pronoun for the bug") is wrong: confuses personal and demonstrative.
